sections.title: Engineering Reliable Automation on n8n
body: n8n is the most flexible automation platform on the market, open-source, self-hostable, and unlimited in what it can connect. But that flexibility is exactly why most teams hit a wall: a few templates work, then the workflows grow brittle, the self-hosting breaks, and no one can tell why a run failed at 3am.

We are an n8n automation agency and development company, not a template reseller. We architect workflows that handle real volume, fail loudly when something goes wrong, and stay maintainable as your operations change. Teams that hire an n8n agency for the first workflow usually come back for the next five, because the automation layer your team gets can actually be relied on.

faqs.question: Can I hire an n8n developer instead of a full agency?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can hire an n8n developer for a scoped workflow build, or bring us in for the audit, build and maintenance together. The free call tells you which fits, and you own the workflows either way.

faqs.question: How much does an n8n agency cost?
faqs.answer: Simple workflow integrations (1-2 systems, basic error handling) typically run $3,000-8,000. Production-grade systems with AI steps, monitoring, and multiple integrations range from $15,000-50,000+ depending on complexity. Ongoing maintenance retainers run $500-2,000/month depending on system size. These are industry ranges; all engagements are scoped after the audit call.

faqs.question: Do you self-host n8n or use n8n Cloud?
faqs.answer: Both. For most teams we recommend self-hosted n8n in queue mode on your infrastructure for control, data ownership, and no per-execution fees. We also work with n8n Cloud when that fits better.

faqs.question: Can you build custom n8n nodes?
faqs.answer: Yes. When n8n's built-in nodes or the community set do not cover an integration or logic you need, we build custom nodes and code steps so you are never blocked by the visual editor.

faqs.question: Can you fix or take over our existing n8n workflows?
faqs.answer: Yes. We audit your current workflows, add error handling, logging, and monitoring, refactor the fragile parts, and document everything so the system is maintainable going forward.

faqs.question: Can n8n run AI agents and LLMs?
faqs.answer: Yes. We embed Claude and other LLMs, RAG retrieval, and agentic steps directly into n8n so your workflows can classify, reason, and take actions, not just pass data between apps.

faqs.question: Who keeps a self-hosted n8n instance patched?
faqs.answer: You do, unless someone is assigned to it. On n8n Cloud, n8n runs the upgrades. On a self-hosted instance, security fixes only reach you when your team upgrades, and n8n publishes them as security advisories on its GitHub repository. Under our maintenance plan we watch those advisories, test each upgrade against your workflows and custom nodes on a staging copy, then upgrade production, so a patch never waits on someone remembering to do it.

faqs.question: Do you maintain n8n after launch?
faqs.answer: Yes. For critical automations we recommend ongoing monitoring, alerting, version upgrades, and maintenance so API changes and n8n updates never silently break operations.

faqs.question: n8n agency vs in-house: which should I choose?
faqs.answer: An in-house n8n hire takes weeks to recruit and ramp up before shipping a single workflow, and you carry the salary whether or not there is enough automation work to fill their time. An n8n agency starts with an audit, ships the first workflow inside the scoped timeline, and includes maintenance as a line item instead of a hope. In-house makes sense once you have enough ongoing n8n work to justify a full-time role.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right n8n agency?
faqs.answer: Ask to see actual self-hosted or production n8n deployments, not just demo screenshots. Check whether error handling, retries, and monitoring are built in by default or sold as an add-on, and confirm maintenance is included after launch. A real n8n agency scopes your systems on an audit call before quoting a number.

faqs.question: How long does it take to hire an n8n agency and launch?
faqs.answer: Booking the audit call takes days. Simple workflow integrations are typically live in one to two weeks after that. Production systems with self-hosting, custom nodes, and AI steps typically take four to eight weeks, timed during the audit.

faqs.question: n8n agency vs n8n development company: is there a difference?
faqs.answer: Not for us. n8n development company and n8n automation agency describe the same engagement: we design the workflow logic, self-host or configure n8n, and stay on for maintenance afterward instead of handing off a one-off build and disappearing.

faqs.question: Do you work with n8n agentur or n8n bureau clients outside the US?
faqs.answer: Yes. Alongside our English-language n8n automation agency work, we support n8n agentur inquiries from German-speaking teams and developpement n8n or n8n bureau requests from French-speaking and MENA clients, through the same audit and build process.

faqs.question: What is n8n good for, and when is it the wrong tool?
faqs.answer: n8n is good for connecting business systems, routing data and running AI steps inside workflows you can self-host and inspect. It is the wrong tool for customer-facing app logic that needs instant responses, or for heavy data processing that belongs in code or a database. We tell you which side your process falls on during the audit call.

faqs.question: What do you build most often with n8n?
faqs.answer: Lead routing and enrichment, CRM and billing syncs, onboarding sequences, document processing, reporting, and AI steps that classify requests or draft replies. Each build includes retries, error alerts and run logs, so a failed API call raises an alert instead of quietly stopping the chain.

faqs.question: How is an n8n agency different from a freelance n8n developer?
faqs.answer: A freelancer often ships the workflow and moves on. We start with a process audit, build error handling and monitoring in by default, document every flow and offer maintenance after launch. Every flow is documented, so your team or a new engineer can pick it up.

faqs.question: How do you stop n8n workflows from failing silently?
faqs.answer: Every workflow gets an error workflow that alerts a named person, retries on temporary API failures and logs each run. On self-hosted n8n we also monitor the instance, queue health and database backups. You hear about a failure from the alert, not from a customer.

faqs.question: Can you move our workflows from another automation tool to n8n?
faqs.answer: Yes. We map each existing workflow, rebuild it in n8n with error handling added, and run old and new side by side until the outputs match. Moving makes sense when per-task fees or data residency rules outgrow your current tool. If they do not, we tell you to stay where you are.

faqs.question: What do you need from us to start an n8n project?
faqs.answer: A short description of the process, the systems it touches and who owns it today. Read access to those tools speeds things up. From the audit we return a workflow map, a hosting plan and a timeline before any build starts.

faqs.question: What is OpenAI Codex and why use it for coding automation?
faqs.answer: Codex is OpenAI's coding agent, available through Codex CLI, that reads a repo, plans changes, and writes code from natural-language intent. We run fleets of these agents to handle PR review, refactors, and test generation inside your real engineering workflow.

faqs.question: Is it safe to give a Codex agent access to our repository?
faqs.answer: Yes, when it is governed properly. Every agent runs in sandboxed isolation with scoped permissions, approval gates, and test checks, so Codex can only act within boundaries you control and nothing untrusted reaches your production branch.

faqs.question: Can Codex be wired into our existing CI/CD pipeline?
faqs.answer: That is exactly what we build. We integrate Codex into your CI/CD so agents run on triggers like new PRs or scheduled refactors, post diffs for human review, and ship only what passes your existing checks and tests.

faqs.question: What coding tasks can you automate with Codex?
faqs.answer: Common builds include PR review agents, large-scale refactors, dependency upgrades and migrations, automated test generation, and repetitive code changes across many files, all running in sandboxed pipelines wired into your stack.

faqs.question: Do we own the Codex agents and pipelines you build?
faqs.answer: Completely. We build inside your repos and infrastructure, and you keep the agents, prompts, and pipelines. There is no lock-in, your team can run and maintain everything after handoff.

faqs.question: Why one engineer instead of a full in-house team?
faqs.answer: Because the engineer is not doing the work alone. They direct a fleet of Codex agents running in parallel across your repos, so you get the output of a small engineering team at the cost and speed of a single senior hire.

faqs.question: What is Codex good at, and where does it fall short?
faqs.answer: Codex is good at well-scoped code changes with a clear test to pass: refactors, dependency upgrades, test generation and repetitive edits across many files. It falls short on vague tasks, code with no tests, and design decisions that need product context. We scope each task so every agent run has a check it must pass.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to hire a Codex expert?
faqs.answer: A placed Codex engineer starts from $60,000 a year, joins your team in 2 to 4 weeks, and comes with a 90-day replacement guarantee and no recruitment fee. A scoped project, where we build the Codex pipeline once and hand it over, is priced after the free audit because the cost depends on how many repos and review gates are involved.

faqs.question: Can I hire a Codex developer instead of an agency project?
faqs.answer: Yes. Through Engineer Placement we place an engineer from our own bench who runs Codex agents on your team, in 2 to 4 weeks, from $60,000 a year, with a 90-day replacement guarantee and no recruitment fee. A scoped project fits better when you only need the pipeline built once.

faqs.question: How is this different from a freelancer or an in-house hire?
faqs.answer: A freelancer usually runs Codex on their own machine, so the setup leaves with them. An in-house hire takes weeks to recruit before any work starts. We build the agent pipeline inside your repo and CI, with sandboxing and review gates, so it keeps working after handoff whoever runs it.

faqs.question: When should we not use Codex agents?
faqs.answer: Hold off when the repo has little test coverage, when the task needs a product decision rather than code, or when nobody on your side can review the pull requests. Agents then produce diffs no one can verify. We often start with test generation to fix the first problem before automating changes.

faqs.question: Do Codex agents merge code on their own?
faqs.answer: No. In the pipelines we build, agents open pull requests and run your checks, and a person approves the merge. Write access is scoped, runs are sandboxed, and anything that fails your tests never reaches review. You can loosen the gates later for low-risk tasks, but we start strict.

faqs.question: What do you need from us to start?
faqs.answer: Repo access for the audit, a short list of the coding work you want automated, and one engineer who can review pull requests. From the audit we return the agent design, the permission scope and the sandbox plan before any agent touches your code.

cards.title: Tables without Row Level Security

faqs.question: Do you set up Row Level Security on Supabase?
faqs.answer: Yes, on every table. RLS is the core of Supabase security, without it, your anon key can expose the whole database. We write, test, and document policies so each row is only readable and writable by who it should be, including multi-tenant isolation.

faqs.question: Can you design or fix our Postgres schema?
faqs.answer: Yes. We design normalized schemas with proper indexes, foreign keys, and version-controlled migrations, and we refactor existing schemas that were never built for scale, without losing your data.

faqs.question: Can you build Supabase edge functions and auth flows?
faqs.answer: Yes. We build Deno edge functions for server-side logic, configure Supabase Auth with custom JWT claims and role-based access, and verify webhooks so your business logic runs securely close to the database.

faqs.question: Can Supabase power RAG and AI features?
faqs.answer: Yes. We use pgvector to turn Postgres into your vector store, storing embeddings, running similarity search, and building RAG pipelines so your product retrieves and reasons over your own data without a separate vector database.

faqs.question: Do you maintain and scale Supabase after launch?
faqs.answer: Yes. For production backends we recommend ongoing monitoring, query and index tuning, connection pooling, backups, and version upgrades so growth and Supabase changes never silently break your app.

faqs.question: How does one engineer secure an entire backend?
faqs.answer: A fleet of agents writes and tests RLS policies, schema migrations, and edge functions in parallel, while the engineer reviews every security-critical decision, so coverage matches a team without the headcount.

faqs.question: What is Supabase good for, and where does it bite?
faqs.answer: Supabase is good for shipping a product fast on real Postgres, with auth, storage, realtime and edge functions included. It bites when tables go live without Row Level Security, when the schema is never designed, or when a service key ends up in client code. Each of these can expose your data.

faqs.question: How do I know if my Supabase project is leaking data?
faqs.answer: Check whether every table in an exposed schema has Row Level Security enabled with policies, whether the service role key appears anywhere in frontend code, and whether storage buckets are public. We run these checks in the audit, then test policies as each user role to confirm what each one can read.

faqs.question: Should we use Supabase or build our own backend?
faqs.answer: Use Supabase when you want Postgres plus auth, storage and realtime without running them yourself. Build your own when you need heavy custom infrastructure or hosting rules Supabase cannot meet. Because Supabase is standard Postgres, moving later is possible, and version-controlled migrations make that easier.

faqs.question: How is this different from hiring a freelance Supabase developer?
faqs.answer: A freelancer often builds features without a security review. We write Row Level Security policies for the tables in scope, test them per role, version every migration and document the data model, so the next developer, ours or yours, can change the backend without reopening holes.

faqs.question: Can you fix a Supabase backend built with Lovable, v0 or Replit?
faqs.answer: Yes. AI-built apps often create tables quickly without access rules or indexes. We audit the schema, add and test Row Level Security, move secrets server-side and add migrations, without rebuilding the frontend you already have.

faqs.question: Do you use pgvector or a separate vector database for AI features?
faqs.answer: For most products, pgvector in the same Supabase Postgres is enough and keeps your data and access rules in one place. We suggest a separate vector database only when volume or query patterns clearly outgrow Postgres, and we say so during the audit, not after the build.

faqs.question: What does a Salesforce implementation consultant do?
faqs.answer: A Salesforce implementation consultant configures the platform to match your sales process, migrates your data from the old system and builds the automation, reports and integrations around it. Good ones also train your team and stay on after go-live, because most adoption problems show up in the first three months.

faqs.question: Do I need a Salesforce implementation partner, or will a consultant do?
faqs.answer: It depends on scope. Large multi-cloud programs with license negotiation often go through a firm from Salesforce's Partner Finder. A Sales Cloud rollout, a migration or an automation project for a B2B team is usually faster with a small senior team. What matters more than the label is whether they map your process before configuring anything.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to hire Salesforce consultants?
faqs.answer: A single focused workflow starts in the low four figures. A full implementation or a multi-tool system is a custom quote after a discovery call, because cost follows the number of users, objects, integrations and how much data has to move. If you want one engineer on it full time, an embedded GTM engineer starts from $60,000/year.

faqs.question: How long does a Salesforce implementation take?
faqs.answer: A focused Sales Cloud setup for one team is weeks, not months. Migrations with years of messy data, several integrations or multiple business units take longer. We set the timeline in the audit, after we have seen your data and your process, and we do not quote one before that.

faqs.question: What does Salesforce automation do?
faqs.answer: Salesforce automation removes repetitive work from the sales process: routing leads, creating follow-up tasks, updating fields when a stage changes, sending approvals and alerts. Done well, reps spend less time on data entry and the CRM stays accurate without anyone chasing them.

faqs.question: What are the types of automation in Salesforce?
faqs.answer: Today the main tool is Flow, which covers record-triggered, scheduled and screen-based automation. Apex code handles logic Flow cannot express. Salesforce has ended support for Workflow Rules and Process Builder, so older orgs should migrate that logic into Flow. Outside the platform, tools like n8n handle cross-system workflows.

faqs.question: Can you give examples of Salesforce automation you build?
faqs.answer: Lead assignment by territory and capacity, enrichment that fills firmographics when a lead is created, tasks generated from buying signals, renewal reminders, deal-desk approvals, and AI research written onto the account before a call. One client now has agents handling pre-call research, CRM updates and lead scoring.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a CRM and sales force automation?
faqs.answer: A CRM stores your customer and deal data. Sales force automation is the set of rules and workflows that act on that data for you, such as routing, reminders and updates. Salesforce does both, but the automation only helps if someone designs it around your process.

faqs.question: Do you offer Salesforce managed services after go-live?
faqs.answer: Yes. After launch we can run admin support, user changes, new Flows, release-readiness checks and integration fixes as a monthly backlog. You get a named engineer who knows your org, not a ticket queue.

faqs.question: Can you migrate us from HubSpot, Pipedrive or Zoho to Salesforce?
faqs.answer: Yes. We map every object and field, clean and deduplicate the data, run a test import in a sandbox, then cut over and reconcile counts. We also rebuild the automations from the old CRM so nothing silently stops working.

faqs.question: Can you fix an existing Salesforce org instead of starting over?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. We audit fields, automations, permissions and reports, remove what nobody uses, consolidate overlapping automation into documented Flows, and fix the data. Starting over is rarely needed and we only suggest it when the audit shows it is cheaper.

faqs.question: Can you connect Salesforce to Clay, outbound tools and AI?
faqs.answer: Yes, that is the part we specialize in. We connect Salesforce to enrichment, email and LinkedIn outreach, billing and support tools through their APIs or n8n, and add AI steps for research, scoring and drafting. Every write back to Salesforce is validated and logged.

faqs.question: Is Salesforce the right CRM for a small team?
faqs.answer: Often not. Salesforce shines when you need complex permissions, many teams or heavy customization. A team of five sellers is usually better served by HubSpot, Pipedrive or Attio, with less admin overhead. We tell you this on the first call.

faqs.question: Who are the best Salesforce consulting firms?
faqs.answer: It depends on what you need: global system integrators for multi-cloud enterprise programs, specialist boutiques for one cloud or one industry, and smaller teams for fast Sales Cloud and automation work. We compare the options honestly in our guide to the best Salesforce consulting firms.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to implement HubSpot?
faqs.answer: HubSpot's own onboarding fee depends on the plan you buy, so check your quote. Our work is separate: A single focused workflow starts in the low four figures. A full implementation or a multi-tool system is a custom quote after a discovery call, because cost follows the number of users, objects, integrations and how much data has to move. If you want one engineer on it full time, an embedded GTM engineer starts from $60,000/year.

faqs.question: What are HubSpot onboarding services?
faqs.answer: HubSpot onboarding services get a new portal from empty to working: pipelines, properties, users and permissions, imported data, the first workflows, and training. Good onboarding also defines lifecycle stages and handoff rules, which is where most portals go wrong.

faqs.question: How long does a HubSpot implementation take?

faqs.question: Can you migrate us from Salesforce, Pipedrive or Zoho to HubSpot?

faqs.question: Is HubSpot CRM still free?

faqs.question: Is HubSpot just a CRM?

faqs.question: What is a Zoho consultant?
faqs.answer: A Zoho consultant sets up and customizes Zoho applications, most often Zoho CRM, migrates data into them and builds automation and integrations. Many write Deluge, Zoho's scripting language, for logic the built-in rules cannot handle.

faqs.question: Do I need a Zoho implementation partner or a consultant?
faqs.answer: For license purchasing and some regional requirements, a firm from Zoho's own partner directory may be needed. For setup, migration, Deluge automation and integrations, what matters is that the person maps your process first and documents what they build. We do that part.

faqs.question: How much does Zoho CRM implementation cost?
faqs.answer: A single focused workflow starts in the low four figures. A full implementation or a multi-tool system is a custom quote after a discovery call, because cost follows the number of users, objects, integrations and how much data has to move. If you want one engineer on it full time, an embedded GTM engineer starts from $60,000/year.

faqs.question: How long does a Zoho CRM implementation take?
faqs.answer: A focused CRM setup for one sales team takes weeks. Projects with Zoho One, several apps and a messy migration take longer. We set the timeline in the audit once we have seen your data.

faqs.question: What is Deluge, and do you write it?
faqs.answer: Deluge is Zoho's own scripting language, used for custom functions, buttons, scheduled jobs and integrations across Zoho apps. Yes, we write it, with error handling and comments so your team can maintain it.

faqs.question: Is Zoho CRM better than Salesforce?
faqs.answer: It depends on scale. Zoho CRM costs less and covers most needs of small and mid-sized teams, especially with Zoho One. Salesforce fits better for complex permissions, many business units and a large partner ecosystem. We help with both and tell you which fits.

faqs.question: What are the downsides of Zoho CRM?
faqs.answer: The interface differs between apps, deeper customization often needs Deluge, and data can end up split across apps if nobody designs the flow between them. Native integrations with outside tools are also thinner than in larger ecosystems. Each of these is fixable with good setup.

faqs.question: Is Zoho a Chinese or Indian company?
faqs.answer: Zoho is an Indian company, headquartered in Chennai. It was founded in 1996 as AdventNet and renamed Zoho Corporation in 2009.

faqs.question: Who is Zoho's biggest competitor?
faqs.answer: In CRM, Zoho mostly competes with Salesforce and HubSpot, plus Pipedrive for smaller sales teams. Zoho's edge is price and the breadth of Zoho One.

faqs.question: Can you migrate us to Zoho CRM from another CRM?
faqs.answer: Yes. We map modules and fields, clean and deduplicate data, run a test import, cut over and reconcile counts, then rebuild the automations from the old system.

faqs.question: Can you integrate Zoho with tools outside Zoho?
faqs.answer: Yes. We connect Zoho CRM to enrichment, outreach, billing, product data and AI models through Zoho's APIs, Deluge and n8n, with logging on every write.

faqs.question: Can you fix our current Zoho setup?
faqs.answer: Yes. We audit fields, rules, blueprints and Deluge functions, remove what is unused, fix data quality and document what stays.

faqs.question: How do I choose a Zoho consultant?
faqs.answer: Ask to see Deluge they wrote, how they handle migrations and whether they integrate tools outside Zoho. Our guide to the best Zoho consultants compares the options.

faqs.question: What does Clay GTM do?
faqs.answer: Clay helps go-to-market teams find, enrich and research prospects. It pulls data from many providers into one table, runs AI research on each row and sends the results to your CRM and outreach tools. Teams use it to build targeted lists and react to buying signals.

faqs.question: What is a Clay agency?
faqs.answer: A Clay agency builds and runs Clay tables for you: enrichment waterfalls, signal tracking, AI research and the integrations into your CRM and outreach tools. Some agencies also run the outbound campaigns that use the data. We do both.

faqs.question: How do you use Clay for GTM?
faqs.answer: Start from your ICP and a trigger, such as hiring or a site visit. Clay finds matching accounts and contacts, enriches them through a waterfall, scores them, writes a first line with Claygent and pushes qualified rows to your CRM and sequencer. The table then refreshes on its own.

faqs.question: What is Claygent used for?
faqs.answer: Claygent is Clay's AI research agent. It visits websites and searches the web to answer a question per row, such as whether a company sells to enterprises or what tools it mentions on its careers page. It works best with tight prompts and a fixed answer format.

faqs.question: Is Claygent expensive?
faqs.answer: Claygent runs on Clay credits, so cost scales with how many rows you research and how heavy each prompt is. Filtering rows by ICP before research and using lighter prompts keeps it affordable. We show you the credit cost per table before it runs at volume.

faqs.question: How much does a Clay agency cost?
faqs.answer: A single focused workflow starts in the low four figures. A full implementation or a multi-tool system is a custom quote after a discovery call, because cost follows the number of users, objects, integrations and how much data has to move. If you want one engineer on it full time, an embedded GTM engineer starts from $60,000/year. Clay credits are billed by Clay to your workspace.

faqs.question: What is a GTM engineer, and do I need one for Clay?
faqs.answer: A GTM engineer builds the systems that connect signals, enrichment, the CRM and outreach. You do not need one to try Clay, but you do once Clay has to run reliably every day. You can hire one through us, or have our team build and run the system.

faqs.question: What does a GTM engineer at Clay earn?
faqs.answer: Salaries vary widely by location and seniority, and Clay does not publish its internal pay bands on this topic. If you are comparing the cost of an in-house hire, an embedded GTM engineer through ManasFlow starts from $60,000/year.

faqs.question: Can Clay push data into HubSpot, Salesforce or Attio?
faqs.answer: Yes. Clay has native CRM integrations, and we use webhooks or n8n when you need custom logic. We add dedupe and ownership rules so Clay updates existing records instead of creating duplicates.

faqs.question: Can Clay send leads to Instantly and HeyReach?
faqs.answer: Yes. Qualified rows go straight into Instantly campaigns or HeyReach lists, with the signal and personalized first line attached. That is how we run our own outbound.

faqs.question: Can you fix our existing Clay tables?
faqs.answer: Yes. We audit your tables, remove wasted enrichment, reorder waterfalls, tighten Claygent prompts and connect the output to your CRM. Most teams cut credit spend and get more usable rows after the cleanup.

faqs.question: Clay vs Apollo: which should we use?
faqs.answer: Apollo is a contact database with built-in sequencing. Clay is a data workflow tool that can use Apollo and many other sources together. Small teams often start with Apollo; teams that need better coverage, signals and custom research move to Clay or use both.

sections.title: Why Most Cold Email Stops Working
body: Cold email still works for B2B. What stopped working is sending the same template to a bought list from your main domain.

cards.title: Deliverability breaks quietly
body: No authentication records, mailboxes sending too much, and no warmup. Emails land in spam and the dashboard still says sent. We set up SPF, DKIM and DMARC, warm mailboxes and cap volume per inbox.

cards.title: Lists without a reason to reach out

faqs.question: What does a cold email agency do?
faqs.answer: A cold email agency sets up and runs outbound email for you: sending domains and mailboxes, lead lists, copy, the campaigns themselves and reply handling. We frame it as outbound automation: we build and run the Instantly and Clay system, and your team takes the conversations.

faqs.question: Is cold email still effective in 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes, for B2B, when it is targeted and timed. Generic templates to bought lists perform worse every year as inbox providers tighten filters. Short emails to the right person, triggered by a real signal and sent from a healthy setup, still start conversations.

faqs.question: What does Instantly.ai do?
faqs.answer: Instantly is a cold email platform. It connects many sending mailboxes, warms them up, rotates sending across them, runs multi-step sequences and collects replies in one inbox. We use it for our own outbound and build client systems on it.

faqs.question: Is Instantly.ai legal and safe to use?
faqs.answer: Instantly is a legitimate, widely used tool. Legality depends on how you send: in the US, CAN-SPAM requires accurate sender details, a physical address and a working opt-out. In the EU and UK, GDPR applies, which usually means a documented legitimate interest and an easy opt-out. We build those rules into every campaign.

faqs.question: How much does a cold email agency cost?
faqs.answer: Our work is a custom quote after a discovery call, because cost depends on volume, the number of segments and how much list building and reply handling we run. A single focused workflow, such as reply routing into your CRM, starts in the low four figures. Tool costs like Instantly and Clay are billed by those vendors to your accounts.

faqs.question: How much does Instantly cost?
faqs.answer: Instantly sells monthly plans based on contacts and emails sent, with lead database and CRM features as add-ons. Prices change, so check instantly.ai/pricing. We help you pick the smallest plan that fits your volume.

faqs.question: Will cold email hurt my company domain?
faqs.answer: Not if it is set up properly. We send from secondary domains with SPF, DKIM and DMARC, warm every mailbox and cap daily volume, so your main domain and its reputation stay out of it.

faqs.question: Do you buy lead lists?
faqs.answer: No. We build lists in Clay from your ICP plus a buying signal, then verify every email before it sends. Bought lists are the fastest way to hurt deliverability.

faqs.question: Do you write the emails?
faqs.answer: Yes. We write short sequences where the first line names the reason we are reaching out, test angles in small batches and keep what earns replies. You approve the copy before anything goes out.

faqs.question: Can you guarantee a number of meetings?
faqs.answer: No, and be careful with anyone who does. Meetings depend on your offer, market and sales follow-up. We report sends, replies and meetings weekly and tune the system around them.

faqs.question: What happens when a prospect replies?
faqs.answer: Each reply is classified, routed to the right owner and logged in your CRM with the full thread. Interested replies trigger a task or deal so someone answers the same day.

faqs.question: Can you combine cold email with LinkedIn outreach?
faqs.answer: Yes. We often run Instantly and HeyReach together on the same lists, so a prospect sees a connection request and an email that refer to the same signal. See our LinkedIn outreach agency page for that side.

faqs.question: What is outbound lead generation?
faqs.answer: Outbound lead generation means reaching out to people who have not contacted you yet, through cold email, LinkedIn or calls, to start sales conversations. It works best when list, timing and message are all specific to the prospect.

faqs.question: How do I choose a cold email agency?
faqs.answer: Ask who owns the domains and mailboxes, how they protect deliverability, where the lists come from, and how replies reach your team. Be wary of fixed meeting guarantees and bought data. Our guide to the best cold email agencies compares the options.

faqs.question: What does a LinkedIn outreach agency do?
faqs.answer: A LinkedIn outreach agency runs prospecting on LinkedIn for you: building target lists, sending connection requests and messages from your team's profiles, following up and passing replies to sales. We build and run that system on HeyReach.

faqs.question: What is LinkedIn outreach?
faqs.answer: LinkedIn outreach means contacting potential buyers on LinkedIn through connection requests, messages and engagement with their posts, to start a sales conversation. It works best when the message refers to something specific about the person or company.

faqs.question: Does LinkedIn outreach still work?
faqs.answer: Yes, when it is targeted and personal. Generic pitches sent right after a connection is accepted get ignored. Short messages tied to a real signal, from a credible profile, still start conversations.

faqs.question: What is HeyReach used for?
faqs.answer: HeyReach is a LinkedIn outreach tool that runs campaigns from several LinkedIn accounts at once, with a shared inbox for replies. Agencies and sales teams use it to spread volume across senders and manage all conversations in one place.

faqs.question: Is HeyReach safe to use?
faqs.answer: LinkedIn's user agreement does not allow third-party automation, so any outreach tool carries some account risk. We lower it by keeping daily limits conservative, spreading volume across accounts and keeping profiles complete and active.

faqs.question: How much does HeyReach cost?
faqs.answer: HeyReach charges per connected sender account per month, with discounts for larger plans. Prices change, so check heyreach.io/pricing. We help you size the number of senders to your target volume.

faqs.question: What is the best tool for LinkedIn outreach?
faqs.answer: It depends on volume. For one person, Sales Navigator and manual messages may be enough. For several senders and campaigns, a tool like HeyReach with a shared inbox makes sense. We use HeyReach and Unipile for our own outreach.

faqs.question: How much does a LinkedIn outreach agency cost?
faqs.answer: Our work is a custom quote after a discovery call, based on the number of senders, segments and how much list building and reply handling we run. A single focused workflow, such as syncing replies into your CRM, starts in the low four figures. HeyReach and data costs are billed to your own accounts.

faqs.question: Whose LinkedIn accounts send the messages?
faqs.answer: Your team's profiles, with their consent. Messages from real people at your company work far better than from unknown profiles. We help tidy each profile before campaigns start.

faqs.question: Can you combine LinkedIn and cold email?
faqs.answer: Yes. We run HeyReach and Instantly from the same lists, so a prospect gets a connection request and an email that refer to the same signal. See our cold email agency page for the email side.

faqs.question: What is the 4-1-1 rule on LinkedIn?
faqs.answer: The 4-1-1 rule is a content guideline: for every six posts you share, four come from others, one is your own original content and one is promotional. It is about posting, not outreach, but active profiles with useful posts get more replies to outreach too.

faqs.question: Can you guarantee meetings from LinkedIn outreach?
faqs.answer: No. Meetings depend on your offer, market and follow-up. We report acceptance rate, replies and meetings weekly and tune the system from there.

faqs.question: How do I choose a LinkedIn outreach agency?
faqs.answer: Ask whose profiles send, how they protect accounts, where lists come from and how replies reach your CRM. Avoid fixed meeting guarantees. Our guide to the best LinkedIn outreach agencies compares the options.

faqs.question: What does an AI agent development agency do?
faqs.answer: An AI agent development agency designs, builds and connects agents to your systems so they complete workflows, not just answer questions. Here that means an architecture audit, agent design, API and tool integration, guardrails and evals, deployment and handoff, run by one senior engineer directing a fleet of AI agents.

faqs.question: Do you offer AI agent development services for a single workflow?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most engagements start with one narrow workflow, such as support triage, CRM enrichment or document processing, so you see a measured result before expanding.

faqs.question: What is the difference between an AI agent and a chatbot?
faqs.answer: A chatbot responds to prompts. An agent can use tools, follow business logic, update systems, and complete workflows with guardrails.

faqs.question: How much does custom AI agent development cost?
faqs.answer: Custom AI agent development is priced per project and scoped after a short architecture audit, not sold as a fixed package. Cost depends on how many workflows you automate, the systems we integrate with, and your security requirements. Most engagements start with one narrow, high-value agent so you see measurable hours saved before expanding.

faqs.question: What do AI agent development services include?
faqs.answer: Our AI agent development services cover the full build: architecture audit, agent design, API and tool integration, private data retrieval, guardrails and evals, deployment, and handoff. We do not sell templates. Each engagement is scoped to your systems and workflows.

faqs.question: Do you offer enterprise AI agent development services?
faqs.answer: Yes. We deliver enterprise AI agent development with private, sandboxed environments, deep API integration into your existing systems, permission and audit controls, and human approval points for high-risk actions. Engagements scale from a single workflow to multi agent systems across departments.

faqs.question: Can agents work with our internal tools?
faqs.answer: Yes. We connect agents to APIs, CRMs, databases, internal docs, and workflow systems while respecting security and permission boundaries.

faqs.question: How do I choose the right AI agent development company?
faqs.answer: Look for an AI agent development company that ships agents into production rather than demos: real tool and API integration, clear guardrails against hallucination, evaluation and testing practices, and a measurable first deliverable. Ask how they scope, test, and hand off the work, and check their case studies for real, verifiable outcomes.

faqs.question: How do you prevent hallucinations?
faqs.answer: We combine scoped tool access, private retrieval, explicit validation steps, evals, and human approval points where the action is high risk.

faqs.question: What can we ship first?
faqs.answer: The first useful agent is usually a narrow workflow: support triage, CRM enrichment, reporting, lead qualification, document processing, or internal operations.

faqs.question: Do you provide AI agent developers, or only fixed-scope projects?
faqs.answer: Both. Most engagements are scoped projects: an audit, a build, and a handoff. If you need a developer embedded on your team building and maintaining agents on an ongoing basis instead, that is placement pricing rather than a project engagement.

faqs.question: Do you offer AI agent consulting services, not just development?
faqs.answer: Yes. The architecture audit is the consulting step: we assess your workflows, tell you honestly where an agent is warranted versus where simpler automation is enough, and only build what is justified.

faqs.question: How long does it take to build a production AI agent?
faqs.answer: Simple agent builds can ship in days. Multi-agent systems and deeper integrations usually take a few weeks depending on the systems you connect, your data access, and testing requirements. We scope the real timeline during the architecture audit, not before it.

faqs.question: Should I hire an AI agent development agency, a freelancer, or build a team in-house?
faqs.answer: It depends on how fast you need the first agent and how much AI engineering you can support internally. An agency fits when you want a working agent without recruiting an AI team first. A freelancer can work for a narrow, one-off build but is a single point of failure if they move on. In-house makes sense once you are running enough agents that you need full-time, dedicated ownership.

faqs.question: What happens after the agent launches?
faqs.answer: You get documentation, access to the code and configuration, and a plan for the next workflow worth automating. Some clients hand off fully at that point. Others keep us on to maintain, monitor, and expand the agent as their systems change.

faqs.question: Why do most AI agent pilots never reach production?
faqs.answer: Most pilots stall because they were built as demos: no real integrations, no test cases, no guardrails and no agreed definition of success. IDC (reported Sept 10, 2026) estimates about 88% of enterprise AI proofs of concept never reach production. We start with an audit that fixes the workflow, the systems and the success criteria before any code, so the build is aimed at production from day one.

faqs.question: How do you make sure an AI agent survives production?
faqs.answer: We test the agent against real cases from your workflow before launch, run it in a sandboxed environment with scoped tool access, and put human approval on high-risk actions. Validation steps and evals catch bad outputs before they reach your systems. You also get documentation and access to the code and configuration, so the agent is not a black box after handoff.

faqs.question: We tried AI before and it did not work. What is different here?
faqs.answer: The usual failure is a chatbot bolted onto a workflow with no access to the systems where the work happens. We scope one narrow workflow in the audit, connect the agent to your APIs, CRM and data, and tie the build to a measurable first deliverable. If a simpler automation fits better than an agent, the audit tells you that instead.

faqs.question: What does the free architecture audit cover?
faqs.answer: The audit maps your workflows, systems and data access, then names the one agent worth building first. It also covers the tools the agent needs, the guardrails and approval points, and what success looks like in numbers. You leave with a scoped plan for the first agent. It starts with a free 30-minute call.

faqs.question: How do you measure whether an AI agent is paying off?
faqs.answer: We agree on the success metric during the audit, usually hours saved, tickets resolved or records processed, and measure the agent against it after launch. That matters: Forrester (via Forkast, Sept 6, 2026) found 41% of AI deployments that reach production show negative ROI after 12 months, most often from unclear success criteria. A measurable first deliverable is how we avoid that.

faqs.question: What happens when the agent gets something wrong?
faqs.answer: High-risk actions wait for a human to approve them, so a wrong decision gets caught before it changes a record, sends an email or moves money. Scoped tool access limits what the agent can touch, and sandboxed compute keeps code execution away from production. Errors that do slip through show up in logs, and we tighten the validation step that missed them.

faqs.question: Who is custom AI agent development not a good fit for?
faqs.answer: It is not a fit if you need a single FAQ chatbot with no actions, since a managed chatbot platform already covers that. It is also not a fit if you cannot give the agent access to the systems it needs to act on, or if you are still unsure whether AI belongs in the workflow at all. Start with the free AI readiness assessment in that case.

faqs.question: Is our data used to train public AI models?
faqs.answer: Your agent runs in a private, sandboxed environment with a private retrieval layer over your own databases and documents. It is not a public chat tool your team pastes data into. Permission and audit controls limit who and what can reach that data, and the audit maps which systems the agent may touch before anything is built.

faqs.question: Do you offer custom workflow automation services for an AI automation agency use case?
faqs.answer: Yes. We build custom workflow solutions on n8n or code, with the AI steps, error handling and monitoring they need. We scope your real systems in an audit first, so nothing is a template.

faqs.question: How does API integration for workflow automation work?
faqs.answer: We connect your systems through their APIs and webhooks, then add retries, deduplication and alerts so a failed call does not silently drop data. Each integration is tested against your real data before go-live.

faqs.question: What workflows can you automate?
faqs.answer: We automate lead routing, reporting, onboarding, support triage, CRM updates, document processing, billing handoffs, and internal operations.

faqs.question: Do you use n8n, Make, Zapier, or custom code?
faqs.answer: We choose the stack based on reliability and control. Many systems use n8n for orchestration plus custom code where templates are too limiting.

faqs.question: How much does custom workflow automation cost?
faqs.answer: Custom workflow automation is scoped after a short architecture audit rather than sold as a fixed package, because cost depends on how many systems you connect and how much custom logic the process needs. A single-workflow build is typically the low four figures; multi-step automation across several tools runs higher and is quoted after the audit.

faqs.question: How do I choose a workflow automation company?
faqs.answer: Look for a workflow automation company that ships production systems, not demo videos: real API integrations, error handling and monitoring, a documented handover, and case studies with verifiable outcomes. Ask how they test a workflow before it touches live data, and what happens when an upstream API changes.

faqs.question: Should we hire an in-house automation engineer instead?
faqs.answer: In-house makes sense once you have enough ongoing automation work to keep one engineer busy full time. Most teams get there gradually, so working with a workflow automation services partner for the build, then deciding on in-house hires once the backlog justifies it, is usually the lower-risk path.

faqs.question: Can you work with messy existing processes?
faqs.answer: Yes. The audit starts by mapping the current process exactly as it works today, then separating what should be automated from what should be redesigned.

faqs.question: Do you maintain workflows after launch?
faqs.answer: Yes. For critical automations we recommend ongoing monitoring, alerts, documentation, and maintenance so API changes do not break operations.

faqs.question: How long does a custom workflow automation project take?
faqs.answer: A single-workflow build usually goes from audit to live system in one to two weeks. Multi-system automation that touches several tools and includes custom logic typically runs four to eight weeks, depending on how many integration points and edge cases need handling.

faqs.question: How is this different from just using Zapier or Make templates?
faqs.answer: Off-the-shelf templates work well when one app talks to one other app on a single trigger. Once the process branches into conditional logic, needs retry handling across several steps, or touches five or more systems, templates get brittle and expensive to run at volume. Custom workflow automation either extends those same platforms with real code or replaces the fragile parts, so the logic matches how your process actually works instead of forcing your process into a template.

faqs.question: Can you migrate an existing Zapier or Make setup, and what does my team need to provide?
faqs.answer: Yes. We audit the existing zaps or scenarios, map what each one does, rebuild the ones that break most often first with proper error handling, and run the new version alongside the old one until it is confirmed reliable before cutting over. From your side, that mostly means an initial audit call, access to the relevant tool accounts or APIs, and short check-ins during the build. We request the minimum access scopes needed for each system and keep credentials in encrypted secrets storage rather than shared documents.

faqs.question: What is the difference between custom workflow automation and custom automation?
faqs.answer: Custom workflow automation connects the tools you already run, so data moves between your CRM, billing, support and reporting systems without manual handoffs. Custom automation is for one process that needs bespoke logic or an AI agent built from scratch. If your pain is copying data between apps, start here. If one process needs judgment, see our custom AI automation page.

faqs.question: What happens when a connected tool changes its API or goes down?
faqs.answer: The workflow retries the failed call, holds the data instead of dropping it, and sends a failure alert so the problem surfaces right away instead of in next month's numbers. Retries, deduplication and alerts are part of every build, not an add-on. On the maintenance plan we monitor the workflows and update them when an upstream API changes.

faqs.question: Which tools can you connect in one workflow?
faqs.answer: Any tool with an API or webhooks. Most builds connect a CRM, a billing or invoicing tool, spreadsheets, a support desk and a reporting dashboard. Niche or legacy software without a native connector is connected with direct API and webhook work instead of CSV exports. The audit lists every integration point before we quote.

faqs.question: Who is custom workflow automation not a good fit for?
faqs.answer: If one app talks to one other app on a single trigger, an off-the-shelf template is cheaper and fine. Custom work pays off once the process branches into conditional logic, needs retry handling across several steps, or touches several systems. The free audit tells you which side of that line your process sits on.

faqs.question: How is this different from hiring a freelancer for one automation?
faqs.answer: The difference shows up after launch. Every build starts with an audit of your real process, ships with error handling, failure alerts and a documented handover, and can move onto a monitored maintenance plan. You are not left with a workflow only one person understands. One senior engineer directs AI agents through the build, so scope stays with one accountable person.

faqs.question: Can you add AI steps to a workflow we already run?
faqs.answer: Yes. We add AI steps where a rule cannot decide, such as support triage, document processing or lead scoring, inside the existing workflow. Each AI step gets the same retries and alerts as the rest of the pipeline, and it is tested against your real data before it touches live records.

faqs.question: Where do the workflows and credentials live after handover?
faqs.answer: In the platform you choose, cloud or self-hosted n8n, or your own infrastructure. Credentials sit in encrypted secrets storage with the minimum access scopes each system needs, never in shared documents. The handover includes documentation of what each workflow does and a maintenance protocol, so your team can see how everything runs.

faqs.question: What do I get from the free 30-minute call?
faqs.answer: We map the manual process you want to remove, the integration points it touches and the workflow that should replace it. You leave knowing whether it is a single-workflow build or a multi-system project, and roughly how long it takes: one to two weeks for one workflow, four to eight weeks for several connected systems.

faqs.question: What is the difference between custom automation and custom workflow automation?
faqs.answer: Custom automation is for one process that needs bespoke logic or an AI agent built around it, such as ticket triage that reads context before acting. Custom workflow automation connects the tools you already run so data moves between them without manual copying. If the pain is judgment inside one process, start here. If it is data stuck between apps, see our custom workflow automation page.

faqs.question: When should a process use an AI agent instead of a fixed workflow?
faqs.answer: Use an agent when a step needs to read context before acting, like a support ticket, an inbound email or a messy form. Use a fixed n8n workflow when the rules never change. Most builds mix both: the workflow handles triggers, retries and system updates, and the agent handles the one step that needs judgment.

faqs.question: Who is custom automation not a good fit for?
faqs.answer: If the task is simple and lives in a single tool, a no-code template is faster and cheaper. Custom work pays off when the logic branches, needs conditional steps, or has to talk to more than two systems. Sometimes the honest answer on the call is that a process should stay manual for now, and we will say so.

faqs.question: How do you test a custom automation before it goes live?
faqs.answer: We run it against real cases from your process before it touches production, including the edge cases your team already knows about. Failures get retries and error handling in the build itself. After launch we keep monitoring, fix edge cases that show up under real usage and extend the logic as the process changes.

faqs.question: How is this different from hiring an in-house automation engineer or a freelancer?
faqs.answer: An in-house hire is slow to find, expensive to keep senior enough to build past basic scripts, and a single point of failure when they leave. With us, one senior engineer directs a fleet of AI agents through audit, build, integration and support, and the automation stays monitored after launch instead of depending on one person.

faqs.question: What should I prepare before the automation call?
faqs.answer: Bring a plain description of the process: what triggers it, which tools it touches, who does it today and where it goes wrong. Screenshots or a sample record help. You do not need a spec. On the call we map the process with you and score which steps are worth automating first.

faqs.question: Can the automation grow after the first build?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most first builds are one narrow workflow, and the same four phases (audit, build, integration, support) apply when you extend it into a multi-agent system later. Because we monitor it after launch, new edge cases and process changes feed straight into the next iteration instead of a new project from zero.

faqs.question: Does custom AI automation replace my team?
faqs.answer: No. It takes over the repeat steps, such as data entry between systems, ticket routing and scheduled reporting, so your team spends its hours on the work only humans should do. Where a decision is risky, we set the agent to draft and a person approves before anything is sent or changed.

We call this context engineering. One senior engineer directs a fleet of AI agents that chunk, index, and wire your data into a retrieval layer your model can actually query, turning scattered documents into an asset your AI can trust.

sections.title: Garbage in, garbage out
body: A powerful model is useless without good context. Without a structured pipeline behind it, your AI hallucinates, and a hallucinated answer inside a business process is a decision made on a lie.

cards.title: Why Generic LLMs Fail in Enterprise Contexts
body: Public AI models are trained on the internet, not on your specific business logic. When asked about your proprietary SOPs, pricing models, or client history, they guess. In a B2B environment, a "guess" is a liability you cannot afford.

cards.title: The Risk of Data Hallucination and Latency
body: Unstructured data leads to slow retrieval times and inaccurate answers. If your AI takes 30 seconds to find a document and then misinterprets it, your automation has failed. You need a system that delivers the truth, instantly.

sections.title: Custom RAG development for precision retrieval

cards.title: How we build it
body: We build the bridge between your private data and your model. The retrieval layer we ship makes sure every response is grounded in your own verified knowledge base, not the model's training data.
items: Semantic Search and Vector Embeddings: We transform your text, PDFs, and databases into mathematical vectors, allowing the AI to understand the "meaning" behind a query, not just keywords.
Real-Time Data Synchronization: Our RAG development services include pipelines that update your vector index the moment your internal documents change. Your AI never works with stale data.
Source Attribution: We configure our systems to cite their sources, giving your team the ability to verify every single claim made by the AI.

sections.title: Enterprise AI infrastructure that scales with your data
body: We do not just connect an LLM to a database. We architect the memory layer underneath it: your data indexed and tuned for speed, security, and relevance as it grows.

cards.title: Vector database setup that holds up at scale
body: Our vector search process helps your AI find the right passage, not just a similar one. We configure vector stores like Pinecone, Weaviate, or Supabase to hold millions of data points at sub-second latency.

figures.label: semantic-data-indexing-optimization

sections.title: The context engineering playbook
body: A RAG pipeline is a precision instrument, not a plugin. We follow the same three-step process on every engagement so your infrastructure delivers accurate results from day one.
The goal is a private knowledge layer your AI can query as reliably as asking your best employee, and it scales across the whole organization.
items: 01. Intelligent Data Chunking: We do not just cut text; we analyze the semantic structure of your documents to preserve meaning across data fragments.
02. Hybrid Search Orchestration: We combine traditional keyword search with modern vector embeddings to capture both technical jargon and natural language intent.
03. RAG Evaluation (RAGAS): We implement continuous testing loops to measure the faithfulness and relevance of the AI's answers, ensuring zero hallucinations before launch.

figures.label: proprietary-information-ai-grounding

faqs.answer: RAG can use internal documents, Notion, Google Drive, databases, support tickets, knowledge bases, PDFs, and structured business data.

faqs.answer: We design retrieval, chunking, evaluation, citations, and guardrails so answers are grounded in approved company data.

faqs.answer: Yes. We can design private retrieval systems with controlled access, secure hosting, and strict boundaries around sensitive data.

faqs.question: Do we need RAG before building agents?
faqs.answer: If agents need to reason over private company knowledge, a reliable retrieval layer usually comes before broad automation.

sections.title: The Enterprise Problem: Open Source Power Without Enterprise Controls
body: OpenClaw gives your agents unlimited access to files, APIs, and network resources by default. For enterprises handling sensitive customer data, financial records, or compliance-regulated workflows, this is a non-starter without proper security infrastructure.

cards.title: Unconstrained Agent Actions
body: Without guardrails, an OpenClaw agent can read any file on the system, make unrestricted network calls, and execute arbitrary processes. A single misconfigured agent could exfiltrate sensitive data or trigger unintended actions across your production environment.

cards.title: Data Privacy and Compliance Gaps
body: Default OpenClaw routes all inference through external APIs with no control over which data leaves your network. For enterprises under GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2, or similar compliance frameworks, this creates unacceptable exposure. You need policy-driven routing that keeps sensitive data on-premises.

faqs.question: What is OpenClaw and how is it different from ChatGPT?
faqs.answer: OpenClaw is an open-source autonomous AI agent that runs locally on your infrastructure. Unlike ChatGPT, which is a cloud-hosted chatbot that responds to prompts, OpenClaw agents plan multi-step tasks, take real actions across your systems (CRM, email, databases), and operate continuously without human intervention.

faqs.question: What does NemoClaw add on top of OpenClaw?
faqs.answer: NemoClaw is our enterprise security stack for OpenClaw, built on NVIDIA's OpenShell sandboxed runtime. It adds a declarative YAML policy engine for controlling network egress, filesystem access, and process execution, plus a privacy router that keeps sensitive data on-device using Nemotron models for local inference.

faqs.question: Do we need NVIDIA GPUs to run NemoClaw?
faqs.answer: NemoClaw is optimized for NVIDIA hardware (RTX GPUs, DGX systems) for local inference with Nemotron models. However, the privacy router can also route non-sensitive inference to cloud providers. We will assess your existing infrastructure and recommend the most cost-effective compute strategy during our discovery phase.

faqs.question: How long does an enterprise deployment take?
faqs.answer: A typical engagement runs 4-8 weeks from discovery to production, depending on the complexity of your compliance requirements and the number of agent workflows. Pilot deployments with a single use case can be live within 2 weeks.

faqs.question: Is NemoClaw compliant with GDPR, HIPAA, and SOC 2?
faqs.answer: NemoClaw provides the infrastructure primitives needed for compliance - sandboxed execution, network egress controls, filesystem isolation, and on-device inference for sensitive data. We write custom YAML policies tailored to your specific compliance framework so that agent behavior stays within your regulatory boundaries.

faqs.question: Can OpenClaw agents integrate with our existing tools?
faqs.answer: Yes. OpenClaw agents can interact with any system that has an API or web interface - including Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, Jira, SAP, internal databases, and custom internal tools. We configure the sandbox policies to whitelist only the endpoints your agents need.

faqs.question: What happens if an agent tries to do something it should not?
faqs.answer: NemoClaw's policy engine enforces a deny-by-default posture. Any action not explicitly whitelisted in the YAML policy - whether a network call, file access, or process execution - is blocked at the runtime level before it can execute. All violations are logged for audit.

faqs.question: Do you provide ongoing support after deployment?
faqs.answer: Yes. We offer dedicated SLA-backed support that includes policy updates as your workflows evolve, monitoring and alerting for agent actions and policy violations, incident response, and scaling support as you expand your agent fleet.

faqs.answer: Start with the audit call: a real agency scopes your actual systems before quoting a number, rather than selling a fixed package sight unseen. Check that they can show working builds, not just slides, and that they stay accountable after launch through a maintenance retainer or handover documentation.

faqs.question: What does an AI automation agency do?
faqs.answer: An AI automation agency, sometimes called an AI automation company, replaces repetitive manual work with systems that run on their own: lead routing, reporting, document handling, support triage, data syncs between the tools you already use. AI matters where judgment is involved, like classifying a message or extracting data from a messy document. We are tool-honest: n8n where it is the fastest reliable path, custom code where the workflow needs more control, and no AI at all where a plain rules-based flow does the job cheaper.

faqs.question: Is an AI automation agency the same as a workflow automation agency?
faqs.answer: Yes, same service, different vocabulary. Both describe an agency that designs and builds systems to remove manual work from your operations. We use n8n for the workflow logic and add an AI agent only where judgment is actually needed, like classifying a message or drafting a reply for review, not everywhere by default.

faqs.question: What does an AI automation agency cost?
faqs.answer: Focused single-workflow builds start in the low four figures and ship in one to two weeks. Full automation systems with AI steps, monitoring, and integrations typically run four to eight weeks and are scoped after the audit call, because the honest answer depends on how many systems the workflow touches. If you need a dedicated engineer embedded full time instead of a scoped project, placement pricing starts from $60,000/year, well under the $150,000+ salary plus roughly $30,000 in benefits a US in-house hire typically costs.

faqs.question: How is an AI automation agency different from hiring in-house?
faqs.answer: An in-house hire costs $150,000+ in salary plus benefits and takes weeks to recruit before they start producing. An agency engagement starts with a scoped audit, builds against your existing stack, and you are not carrying a full-time salary, payroll taxes, or a hiring pipeline for a role you may only need part of the time.

faqs.question: How is this different from hiring a freelancer?
faqs.answer: A freelancer builds the happy path. We build the happy path plus error handling, retries, monitoring, and documentation, and stay accountable for the system after launch. That difference is invisible in the demo and decisive in month three.

faqs.question: Do you use AI in every automation?
faqs.answer: No. AI adds cost and variance, so it only goes where judgment is involved: classification, extraction from messy input, or drafting for human review. Deterministic steps stay deterministic.

faqs.question: Can I just use a no-code tool myself instead of hiring an agency?
faqs.answer: For a single simple trigger, yes, a no-code tool alone can work. Most teams come to an agency once the workflow needs conditional logic across more than two systems, error handling, or an AI agent making decisions, which is where DIY no-code setups tend to break down.

faqs.question: How long does an AI automation agency engagement take?
faqs.answer: A single focused workflow is typically live in one to two weeks. A full automation system, with an AI layer, monitoring, and integrations across multiple tools, typically takes four to eight weeks and is timed during the audit call.

faqs.question: Can you work with our existing tech stack?
faqs.answer: Yes. We connect the CRM, database, spreadsheets, email, Slack, and private APIs you already run rather than forcing a new stack. Most builds are integration-heavy by design.

faqs.question: What happens after the automation ships? Do you maintain it?
faqs.answer: Either a clean handover with documentation and a working session for your team, or a maintenance retainer where we watch the monitors, handle API changes, and extend the system as your process evolves.

faqs.question: Is an AI automation agency the same as an AI agent development company?
faqs.answer: They overlap. Agent development is one of the services an automation agency delivers, building autonomous agents for complex logic, alongside workflow automation, API integration, and RAG pipelines. If you already know you need an agent specifically, our AI agent development page covers that scope in detail.

faqs.question: What's the difference between an AI automation agency and an automation consultant?
faqs.answer: A consultant typically advises and hands you a recommendation. An agency scopes the audit, then builds and ships the system itself. We do both under one team: the audit call is the consulting step, and the build plus maintenance is the agency work, instead of a hand-off between two separate vendors.

faqs.question: Do you work with companies in the USA, or only internationally?
faqs.answer: Both. Every engagement is remote-first: the audit call, the build, and ongoing maintenance happen over video and your existing tools. We work with teams across the USA on US business hours and with international teams the same way, so location does not change the engagement.

faqs.question: Are you a B2B AI automation agency, or do you also build consumer apps?
faqs.answer: B2B. Our engagements automate internal operations and customer-facing workflows for companies, not consumer social apps. Most clients are SaaS platforms, ecommerce operators, agencies, and internal operations teams removing manual work from processes their own staff or customers run into daily.

faqs.question: Do you build automations for SaaS and ecommerce companies specifically?
faqs.answer: Yes, alongside other B2B teams. SaaS companies typically automate onboarding, usage checks, and support triage. Ecommerce operators automate order handling, inventory syncs across channels, and customer service. Both run through the same audit, build, maintain model as every other engagement.

faqs.question: Is this different from IT automation or CRM automation specifically?
faqs.answer: No, it's the same underlying work described with different vocabulary. IT systems and CRM automation are two of the systems we connect into a workflow, alongside your database, spreadsheets, email, and internal APIs, scoped to your engagement.

faqs.question: How do I find the best AI automation agency for my business?
faqs.answer: Pick the one that scopes your systems before it quotes, shows working builds instead of slides, and stays accountable after launch. Ask how they handle errors, retries and monitoring, and who fixes the workflow when an API changes. If the answer is a fixed package sold before anyone has seen your stack, keep looking. Our comparison of AI automation agencies lists what to check.

faqs.question: What is the smallest project I can start with?
faqs.answer: One focused workflow. It starts in the low four figures and is typically live in one to two weeks, with error handling, retries and monitoring built in. Most teams start there, see it run on their own data, then expand into a full system with AI steps once the first workflow has proved itself.

faqs.question: What happens if the automation does not work?
faqs.answer: We do not call a build done until it runs on your real data inside your systems. Every build is tested in a sandbox first, then shipped with error handling, retries and monitoring. After launch you choose a documented handover or a maintenance retainer, where we watch the monitors and fix breakage when an API or edge case changes.

faqs.question: What does an AI workflow automation agency build first?
faqs.answer: The workflow the audit shows pays for itself fastest. That is usually lead routing, reporting, document handling, support triage or a data sync between two tools your team copies between by hand. AI is added only at the steps that need judgment, like classifying a message or pulling fields out of a messy document.

faqs.question: Is an AI implementation agency different from an AI automation agency?
faqs.answer: Mostly the name. Both should take AI from idea to a system your team uses every day. The hard part is production: IDC data reported by bex.co in September 2026 puts about 88% of enterprise AI proofs of concept as never reaching production. We scope, build, deploy into your systems and maintain, so the work does not stop at a demo.

faqs.question: Who is an AI automation agency not a good fit for?
faqs.answer: Teams with one simple trigger a no-code tool already handles, teams that need a full-time engineer embedded rather than a scoped project, and teams not ready to give access to the systems the automation must touch. In those cases we will say so on the audit call and point you to Forward Deployed Engineers or a DIY setup instead.

faqs.question: Which tools do you build automations with?
faqs.answer: n8n for triggers, webhooks and workflow logic, Claude Code and custom code for logic a trigger cannot handle, and RAG pipelines when answers must come from your own data. We connect into the CRM, database, spreadsheets, email, Slack and private APIs you already run instead of moving you onto a new stack.

faqs.question: Do you build an AI chatbot for a website or for WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Both, plus helpdesk and internal-knowledge bots. The channel changes the integration, not the method: retrieval that grounds answers in your data, tools that update your CRM or helpdesk, and a clear hand-off to a human. faqs.question: Can an AI chatbot developer work in French or Arabic as well as English?
