faqs.question: What does an AI chatbot development agency actually do?
faqs.answer: A chatbot development agency designs and builds the LLM chatbot end to end: the conversation flow, the retrieval layer that grounds answers in your data, the tool calls that let the bot take action instead of only responding, and the escalation logic for when it should hand off to a human. The build is only half the job. The agency should also cover the eval harness that catches regressions and the maintenance plan that keeps the bot useful as your data and models change.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to hire an AI chatbot development agency?
faqs.answer: A simple FAQ chatbot on a managed platform can launch for under $10,000. Custom LLM chatbots with retrieval and integrations typically run in the low five figures to start, scoped after an audit call, because the honest number depends on how many systems the bot needs to read from and write to. Enterprise programs with compliance, multi-channel deployment, and ongoing maintenance run well past six figures.

faqs.question: How do I choose between a chatbot agency and a managed chatbot platform?
faqs.answer: A managed platform trades flexibility for speed: faster to launch, vendor-supported, but you are limited to the retrieval, integrations, and logic the platform already ships. A custom build from an agency costs more upfront but gives you full control over retrieval, prompts, tool calls, and the exact systems the bot touches. Most teams start with a platform for a single simple FAQ flow and move to a custom build once the bot needs to read from more than one internal system.

faqs.question: Is a chatbot marketing agency the same as a chatbot development agency?
faqs.answer: No. A chatbot marketing agency typically builds lead-capture and campaign bots that live on a landing page or ad flow. A chatbot development agency builds the underlying LLM system: the model, the retrieval, the integrations, and the maintenance behind it. ManasFlow is a development agency, not a marketing shop; the chatbots we build are wired into your CRM and helpdesk, not just a lead form with a chat skin on top.

faqs.question: Do you build AI chatbots for websites, or only internal tools?
faqs.answer: Both. A website chatbot needs the same underlying architecture as an internal one: retrieval grounded in your docs or product data, escalation to a human when the bot hits its limit, and a maintenance plan so answers stay accurate as your site and product change. We scope the surface, website widget, in-app assistant, or internal tool, during the audit call rather than assuming one template fits every use case.

faqs.question: What is a conversational AI chatbot agency, and is that different from what you do?
faqs.answer: Conversational AI is the broader term for chat, voice, and messaging systems that hold context across turns. A chatbot is one surface for that same underlying technology. We build the LLM layer, the retrieval, and the integrations that make conversational AI work in text-based chat; if you need voice specifically, that is a separate scoping conversation.

faqs.question: Do you use AI in every part of the chatbot, or just the reply?
faqs.answer: The reply is the visible part, but the retrieval step that finds the right information and the classification step that routes intent are just as important, and both benefit from the same LLM. Where a plain rules-based flow does the job, we do not add AI just to add it: a chatbot that only needs to answer three fixed questions does not need a full retrieval pipeline.

faqs.question: Can the chatbot integrate with our CRM and helpdesk specifically?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it should. A chatbot that cannot look up a contact, create a ticket, or update a deal is leaving most of its value on the table. We wire chatbots into Salesforce, HubSpot, Zendesk, Intercom, and internal APIs as part of the standard build, not as a separate add-on.

faqs.question: How long does it take to build and ship an AI chatbot?
faqs.answer: A focused, well-scoped chatbot MVP typically ships in four to eight weeks. Production hardening, integrations, evals, observability, and escalation logic, adds another four to eight weeks. Most production-ready chatbots take two to four months from kickoff.

faqs.question: What happens after the chatbot launches? Do you maintain it?
faqs.answer: Either a clean handover with documentation, or a maintenance retainer where we keep tuning prompts and retrieval as your data grows, rerun evals to catch regressions, and update the bot as language models improve. A chatbot without a maintenance plan tends to drift within months as user intent and your underlying data change.

faqs.question: Do you offer multilingual chatbot delivery?
faqs.answer: Yes, English, French, and Arabic, which makes us a fit for EU, MENA, and bilingual North American teams that struggle to find a chatbot partner who delivers cleanly in their users' first language rather than machine-translating an English-only bot.

faqs.question: Is this different from hiring a freelancer to build a chatbot?
faqs.answer: A freelancer typically builds the happy path: the bot answers the questions it was designed for. We build the happy path plus retrieval grounding, escalation logic, an eval harness, and a maintenance plan, and stay accountable for the system after launch. That difference does not show up in a demo; it shows up three months in, when the underlying data has changed and the bot either keeps up or does not.

sections.title: What a workflow automation agency actually does
body: What it is

A workflow automation agency turns a manual business process into a system that runs itself: lead handoffs, approval chains, document processing, data syncs between the CRM, billing, spreadsheets, and Slack. The goal is not to remove people from the process. It is to remove the mechanical steps so people only handle the judgment calls.

The difference between a connected app and a production workflow is everything around the happy path: retries, idempotency, dead-letter queues, alerting, and a documented answer to "what happens when this step fails at 2am". That surrounding engineering is most of the work and most of the value, and it is exactly what quick integration jobs skip.

We are tool-honest about how we build. n8n covers most workflows fastest and keeps them editable by your team. When a workflow needs more control, tighter performance, or logic n8n handles badly, we write custom TypeScript or Python. And when a process is too unstable to automate yet, we say so and tell you what to fix first.

Most agencies in this category are platform resellers first: they sell you a Zapier or Make subscription and call the setup the service. We are engineers first. The workflow itself is the deliverable, not a license fee, and it is built to survive the API change, the traffic spike, and the malformed record that a template-based setup was never tested against.

faqs.question: What does workflow automation cost with an agency?
faqs.answer: A focused single-workflow build starts in the low four figures and ships in one to two weeks. Multi-step systems that touch several tools typically run four to eight weeks. faqs.question: Why not just hire a cheaper freelancer to connect the apps?
faqs.answer: For a simple two-app sync, you probably should, and we will say so on the call. The gap shows up on workflows that matter: a freelancer builds the happy path, while we build the happy path plus retries, monitoring, documentation, and someone accountable when an API changes in month three.

faqs.question: Do you build on n8n or write custom code?
faqs.answer: Both, chosen per workflow. n8n is the default because it is fast, reliable, and your team can read the flows. We drop to custom TypeScript or Python when a workflow needs performance, complex branching, or logic that fights the visual editor.

faqs.question: Can our team maintain the workflows ourselves?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we design for that. Handover includes a runbook, alert setup, and a working session with your team. If you would rather not own it, we run a maintenance retainer and watch the monitors for you.

faqs.question: How do you decide what not to automate?
faqs.answer: Anything that changes weekly, runs rarely, or requires judgment without a clean review path stays manual. Part of the audit is telling you which steps fail that test. Automating the wrong step costs more than not automating at all.

faqs.question: n8n vs Zapier vs Make: which do you build on?
faqs.answer: n8n by default, because it is self-hostable, your team can read the flows, and it does not meter you by task the way Zapier and Make do at volume. We will build on Zapier or Make instead when a client already runs one and switching costs more than it saves. The platform is a means to a reliable workflow, not the pitch.

faqs.question: Is this the same thing as RPA?
faqs.answer: Related but different. RPA usually means bots clicking through a legacy UI because there is no API. Most of what we build talks to APIs directly, which is faster and more stable. When a system genuinely has no API, we will say so and scope UI-level automation honestly rather than pretend every process fits the API-first model.

faqs.question: How do I choose a workflow automation agency?
faqs.answer: Ask what happens when the workflow fails at 2am, not just how fast they can wire two apps together. A workflow automation agency worth hiring can show you retries, idempotency, alerting, and a real answer for what breaks first at higher volume, plus which platform they would not recommend for your case. If every answer is "yes we can build that," that is the gap that costs you later.

faqs.question: What is a workflow automation agency?
faqs.answer: A workflow automation agency turns a manual business process into software that runs on its own, such as lead handoffs, approval chains, document processing and data syncs between your CRM, billing, spreadsheets and Slack. The work includes the parts around the happy path: retries, idempotency, alerting and a documented answer for what happens when a step fails.

faqs.question: How long does it take to automate a workflow?
faqs.answer: A single workflow typically goes live in one to two weeks. A multi-step system covering a full process usually takes four to eight weeks. We ship the highest-value step first, then harden it against real historical data before expanding, so you have something working in production early instead of waiting for one big rollout.

faqs.question: What do you need from our team to get started?
faqs.answer: Time with the people who run the process today, and access to the tools the workflow touches. During process mapping we walk the workflow end to end with them and score each step by frequency, friction and how clear the rules are. Steps that need judgment stay with your team.

faqs.question: Can you fix a Zapier or n8n workflow someone else built?
faqs.answer: Yes. A workflow that already failed silently and cost you data or a customer is a common starting point. We review what exists, keep what works, and rebuild the fragile parts with the error handling, deduplication and alerts they should have had. If the process itself is unstable, we tell you to fix that first.

sections.title: What a no-code development agency actually does
body: What it is

A no-code development agency builds working software on visual platforms: an app on Bubble or Lovable, an interface generated with v0, workflows on n8n. Done right, no-code compresses months of development into weeks and leaves you with something your own team can open and understand. That speed is real, and for a large class of products it is the correct engineering decision, not a compromise.

The dishonesty in this market is pretending no-code has no ceiling. It does: complex data models, heavy computation, strict performance needs, and some compliance setups all push past what visual platforms handle well. Because we build with code every week, we can tell you which side of that line your project is on during the first call, instead of discovering it in month four.

Our default is hybrid: no-code where it fits, code where it does not. A Bubble front end over a Supabase database. An n8n workflow calling a small custom service for the one step n8n does badly. A Lovable or v0 start that gets hardened into a real Next.js codebase when traction demands it. You get no-code speed without betting the company on a platform ceiling.

Most no-code agencies specialize in one platform and recommend it regardless of fit, because that is the tool they know how to sell. We are not a Bubble shop or a Webflow shop; we are a build shop that happens to use no-code tools well and code just as well, so the platform recommendation you get is not tied to what we have to sell you.

faqs.question: Are you a no-code-only shop?
faqs.answer: No, and that is deliberate. We write production code every week, which is why our no-code recommendations are trustworthy: we have no incentive to force your project into a platform it has outgrown before it starts.

faqs.question: What happens if we outgrow the no-code platform?
faqs.answer: We plan for it up front. Builds are structured so the data layer can move to Supabase and hot paths can move to code without a full rewrite. Outgrowing no-code is a good problem; the goal is to make the migration boring.

faqs.question: Can our team maintain the build themselves?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and that is one of no-code's real advantages. Handover includes documentation and a working session. n8n workflows especially are readable by ops people, not just developers. If you would rather not own it, we run a maintenance retainer.

faqs.question: Bubble, Webflow, or Xano: which platform is right for us?

Xano fits when you need a standalone no-code backend and API layer under a separate front end. We recommend the fit on the first call, even when the answer is a platform we do not build on.

faqs.answer: Platform specialists can be efficient for the platform they know, but efficient is not the same as correctly scoped. A no-code agency with only one platform in its toolkit has no incentive to say your project has outgrown it. Ask to see a build they migrated out of no-code, not just ones they kept in it.

faqs.answer: Use them; they are good at what they cover, and we build with them rather than around them. They stop at their own walls: they cannot orchestrate across your whole stack, dedupe between systems, or run AI steps with review queues. If your needs genuinely fit inside one tool, we will tell you that on the call and save you the engagement.

faqs.question: Will AI be writing our marketing content?
faqs.answer: Drafting, yes, where it helps: variants, personalization, and repurposing. Publishing, no. Everything AI writes passes a human review queue before it touches your audience. We build the queue into the workflow so review is a click, not a chore.

faqs.question: Do we need to change our martech stack?
faqs.answer: Almost never. The whole approach is building connective tissue between the CRM, email platform, ad accounts, and analytics you already pay for. If something in the stack is genuinely the problem, we will say so, but replacing tools is the last resort, not the pitch.

faqs.question: How do you measure whether the automation worked?
faqs.answer: Every build ships with its own metric wired in before launch: speed-to-lead, campaign send accuracy, hours removed from content ops. We instrument with PostHog and your existing analytics, and you see the numbers we see.

faqs.question: How do I choose a marketing automation agency?
faqs.answer: Ask what they build versus what they resell. A marketing automation agency should show real API integrations, deduplication and monitoring on lead flow, a human review step on anything AI drafts, and case studies with verifiable numbers, not a slide deck of a platform's own features. If they cannot explain what happens when an upstream API changes, that is the gap that breaks your pipeline later.

faqs.question: Should we hire in-house instead of an agency?
faqs.answer: In-house makes sense once your marketing ops backlog is large enough to keep someone busy full time on integrations and monitoring. Most B2B and SaaS teams are not there yet, so an agency build for the initial lead routing and lifecycle systems, followed by a maintenance retainer or an in-house hire once the workload justifies it, is usually the lower-risk path.

faqs.question: What makes this an AI marketing automation agency and not just a marketing automation agency?
faqs.answer: AI does specific jobs inside the system, not the whole job: scoring and classifying leads by real signal instead of a static point scale, personalizing outreach at a depth templates cannot reach, and drafting content and campaign variants. Every one of those outputs passes a human review queue before it reaches a customer. That is different from a platform pitched as AI-powered that auto-sends without a person in the loop.

faqs.question: Are you a HubSpot or Marketo consultancy?
faqs.answer: No. HubSpot and Marketo partner agencies are good at configuring those specific platforms, and if that is genuinely all you need, hire one. We are engineers who build the plumbing between whatever platforms you already run, including HubSpot or Marketo, so the automation is not capped at what one vendor's workflow builder can do.

faqs.question: What is a B2B marketing automation agency?
faqs.answer: A B2B marketing automation agency builds the systems that move leads and campaign data between your tools without manual work. That means enrichment, scoring and routing of inbound leads, lifecycle emails triggered by product events, and reporting synced from ad and analytics platforms. We build on n8n and your existing CRM, with monitoring so the flows keep running after launch.

faqs.question: How long does it take to set up marketing automation?
faqs.answer: The first automation, usually lead routing, goes live in one to two weeks. A full marketing ops system covering lead flow, lifecycle triggers, content ops and reporting typically takes four to eight weeks. We ship one flow at a time in order of value, so you see a working result before the larger system is finished.

faqs.question: Which tools do you use for marketing automation?
faqs.answer: n8n for orchestration, the Claude API for scoring, classification and drafting, PostHog for product events and measurement, and Supabase when a flow needs its own data store. Around that sits the CRM, email platform and ad accounts you already run. We connect to them through their APIs rather than asking you to migrate.

faqs.question: What happens when a marketing workflow breaks?
faqs.answer: Every flow ships with retries, deduplication and failure alerts, so a timed-out API call or a malformed lead gets caught instead of silently dropped. After launch your team gets a runbook and a working session. If you would rather not own that, a maintenance retainer has us watching the monitors and handling API changes.

faqs.question: What happens on the free marketing ops audit call?
faqs.answer: It is 30 minutes. We trace one lead and one campaign through your current stack, find where hours and data leak, and tell you which fixes are worth automating and which are not. You leave with a short priority list. If your needs fit inside one tool you already own, we say so and you skip the engagement.

faqs.question: Who is marketing automation not a good fit for?
faqs.answer: Teams without consistent lead flow, teams that want AI to publish without human review, and teams about to replace their CRM or email platform. In the first case there is nothing to route yet. In the second we will not build it. In the third, migrate first, then automate, or you pay for the same plumbing twice.

faqs.answer: Yes. Our marketing operations automation case study reports 95% of tasks automated, and it is linked on this page. We publish only results a client build actually produced. On the audit call we will tell you which parts of that build apply to your stack and which do not.

sections.title: What Next.js AI app development involves
body: What it is

Next.js is the default frame for serious AI products right now, and for concrete reasons: server components keep API keys and heavy retrieval off the client, streaming is native so model output renders as it generates, and Vercel's infrastructure handles the spiky, long-running request patterns AI workloads create. When someone asks us what to build an AI app on, this stack is usually the honest answer, and it is the one we use for our own site.

The AI layer is where most projects quietly fail. A RAG pipeline that looks brilliant on ten test questions falls apart on real user phrasing; an agent that worked in the demo loops on an edge case in front of a customer. Production AI needs an eval set that catches regressions before users do, confidence thresholds with fallback paths, human review where stakes are high, and per-feature cost tracking so one power user cannot torch your margin.

We build the whole thing as one system: the Next.js app, the Supabase data layer with row-level security, the Claude integration with structured outputs and tool use, and PostHog analytics wired to the AI features so you know what users actually do with them. One team, strategy through maintenance, and we will tell you when a feature does not need AI at all.

Most Next.js agencies prove their App Router and React Server Components depth with a content site or a headless-CMS build, which is real skill but a different job. Our production surface is the AI layer on top of that same framework knowledge: server components keeping model calls and retrieval off the client, streaming that does not jank under a real model's latency, and an architecture built to survive traffic spikes an AI feature can cause overnight.

sections.title: What RevOps automation covers
body: What it is

RevOps owns the process and the data, and spends much of its time repairing both. Duplicate accounts, missing fields, leads routed to the wrong rep, stale opportunities. Each is small. Together they undermine every report.

sections.title: Three Layers of an Agent That Actually Resolves
body: A co-pilot that only answers questions will not move your deflection rate. What moves it is a system that takes the action itself, and knows when not to.
Full architecture write-up, including the RAG and guardrail detail, lives on our guide to how AI customer support agent development works .

cards.title: Knowledge layer (RAG)
body: The agent retrieves passages from your help center, policy docs, and past tickets at the moment of the question, then answers using only that retrieved context. This is the single most effective defense against made-up answers.

cards.title: Tool layer
body: Order lookups, refunds, and ticket handoffs are functions the agent can call, not scripted replies. It decides which tool fits, fills in the parameters, and uses the result to compose its answer.

cards.title: Escalation layer
body: Every response runs a confidence check. Below the threshold, or on an unclear rule, the agent hands off to a human with full context attached, instead of guessing.

faqs.question: What is the difference between an AI chatbot and an AI customer support agent?
faqs.answer: A chatbot follows fixed scripts and decision trees. An AI customer support agent uses a language model grounded in your knowledge base through RAG, calls tools to take real actions like order lookups and refunds, and decides on its own when to escalate to a human. The agent resolves requests end to end; a chatbot mostly routes or answers from a fixed menu.

faqs.question: How much can an AI support agent actually deflect?
faqs.answer: Median enterprise tier-1 deflection is around 41 percent, with the top quartile near 59 percent, per Zendesk and Salesforce benchmarks. High-volume, rule-based intents like order status and password resets deflect at 70 percent or more; nuanced complaints rarely exceed 25 percent. Your blended rate depends on your ticket mix, which is what we scope in the audit.

faqs.question: Will it give customers wrong answers?
faqs.answer: It can, but the risk is controllable, and it is mostly a data problem, not a model problem. We ground every answer in your knowledge base with RAG, force the agent to cite sources, set a confidence threshold that escalates uncertain cases, and keep your documentation clean. Guardrails like these cut hallucination risk substantially compared with an ungrounded model.

faqs.question: Should we buy a platform like Intercom Fin or build a custom agent?
faqs.answer: Buy a platform when your support maps to common patterns and you want a fast start; Fin runs about $0.99 per resolved conversation with no setup fees on an existing helpdesk. Build custom when you need deep integration with internal systems a platform cannot reach, unusual business logic, full data control, or better unit economics at high volume, since a small per-resolution price difference adds up fast past 100,000 monthly resolutions. Many teams start on a platform and move specialized flows to a custom build once the economics are clear.

faqs.question: Does it integrate with Zendesk, Intercom, Salesforce, or HubSpot?
faqs.answer: Yes. We connect through the same helpdesk APIs platform agents use, and can also reach systems a platform cannot: an internal billing service, a proprietary order database, or a custom CRM. Each action becomes a tool the agent can call, scoped to only what you permit.

faqs.question: How is this different from your AI chatbot development agency service?
faqs.answer: AI chatbot development is the underlying build: the conversation flow, retrieval, and tool-calling architecture for any chat surface, a website widget, an in-app assistant, an internal tool. This page is the applied version specifically for customer support: ticket resolution, order/refund actions, and the deflection, CSAT, and cost-per-resolution economics that matter for a support team. If your need is a general-purpose chatbot rather than a support agent measured against ticket volume, start with AI Chatbot Development Agency instead.

faqs.question: What does it cost?
faqs.answer: Platforms charge per resolution or per seat: Fin runs about $0.99 per resolved conversation with a $49.50 monthly minimum; Zendesk adds an AI add-on around $50 per agent per month on top of seat pricing. A custom build carries higher upfront engineering cost but a lower marginal cost per resolution since you pay for hosting and inference, not a per-outcome fee. We scope a real number after the audit, once we know your ticket volume and systems.

faqs.question: How do you measure if it's actually working?
faqs.answer: Deflection rate (share resolved without a human), resolution rate (the stricter version, confirmed fully answered), CSAT, and cost per resolution, tracked together. Rising deflection with falling CSAT is a warning sign that escalation logic is too aggressive, not a win. We set up this tracking as part of the build, not as an afterthought.

sections.title: What AI integration services include
body: What it is

An integration has three jobs. Get the right data to the model at the right moment. Take the model's output and turn it into a valid change in a system of record. And survive the ordinary failures: rate limits, timeouts, schema changes and duplicate events.

We use existing APIs, webhooks and exports where they exist. When an integration touches customer or financial records, writes go through validation and are logged, so a bad output produces a rejected write instead of a corrupt record.
We also put results where people already work. An AI feature inside the existing product gets used. One in a separate dashboard often does not.

title: Build or buy your AI agent? Decide on these five questions
description: Build vs buy AI agents: buy when a tool does 80% of the job and reaches your data. Five questions on fit, cost, control and upkeep, plus two calculators.
intro: Build vs buy AI agents
note: Free 30-min call. No pitch, no slides.

sections.title: How to decide between building and buying
body: What it is

Buying wins when the job is common, the tool connects to your systems and the price scales acceptably with your usage. Support answers from a help center and meeting notes are typical. Building wins when the job depends on your own data and permissions, when the tool cannot write to your systems, or when usage cost or lock-in becomes the main problem.

Five questions settle most cases. Does an existing tool do at least 80% of the job out of the box? Can it reach the systems and data the job needs, with the permissions you require? What does it cost at your expected volume in twelve months, not today? Who maintains it when a model, an API or the process changes? And how much control do you need over data, logging and behavior?
If the honest answer to the first two is yes, buy. If it is no to either, a custom agent is worth scoping. If it is mixed, a small custom layer on top of a bought tool is often the cheapest path.

A process is a chain of decisions and handoffs. Before automating it, we write down each step, who does it, which system holds the input and what happens when the input is wrong. Half the value often comes from removing steps nobody needed.

sections.title: Why AI coding tools become security liabilities
body: Claude Code and tools like it ship with permissive defaults built for a single developer. Rolled out across a team without hardening, those defaults create categories of risk most engineering leaders only discover after an incident.

cards.title: Secret & Credential Exposure
body: AI coding agents read your entire codebase - including .env files, private keys, and database connection strings - and send that context to external inference APIs. Without explicit exclusion rules, your secrets leave your network with every prompt.

cards.title: Prompt Injection via Malicious Files
body: An attacker who can place a file in your codebase can embed hidden instructions that Claude Code will execute when it reads that file. Third-party packages, client-submitted code, and public READMEs are all potential injection vectors.

cards.title: Auto-Approval of Dangerous Actions
body: Claude Code's YOLO mode and MCP server integrations can execute shell commands, make network requests, and modify files without developer confirmation. One misconfigured permission scope in a production environment can cause irreversible damage.

faqs.question: What does an AI code security audit cover?
faqs.answer: We review code and configuration produced with AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Copilot and Cursor: exposed secrets, prompt injection paths, MCP server trust, permissive agent settings and dependency risk. You receive a written report and a hardened configuration package.

faqs.question: Do you offer AI-generated code audit services for a codebase that is already live?
faqs.answer: Yes. Send the repo scope and the tools your team used. The free call confirms what we would check and what a fix pass looks like before you commit to anything.

faqs.question: Is Claude Code a security risk for enterprise teams?
faqs.answer: Claude Code is a powerful tool but ships with permissive defaults: it can read any file it can access, execute shell commands, and send your code to Anthropic's API. Without a hardened configuration, sensitive files like .env secrets, private keys, and internal architecture documents can end up in the AI's context window and transmitted externally. With the right setup - .claudeignore, command allowlists, and approval gates - these risks are manageable.

faqs.question: What is prompt injection in AI coding agents?
faqs.answer: Prompt injection is when an attacker embeds hidden instructions inside a file, comment, or README that Claude Code reads. When the agent processes that file, it may execute the attacker's instructions - exfiltrating data, modifying code, or running unauthorized commands - believing them to be legitimate user requests. It is the most critical and underappreciated risk in AI-assisted development.

faqs.question: How do I prevent Claude Code from reading my .env files?
faqs.answer: The most direct fix is adding .env and credential files to your .claudeignore configuration. This explicitly tells Claude Code to skip those files when exploring your codebase. You should also add secrets directories, private key files, and any files containing database connection strings. We configure a properly scoped .claudeignore as part of the hardening engagement.

faqs.question: What is YOLO mode and why is it a security concern?
faqs.answer: YOLO mode (surfaced in the Claude Code source leak as classifyYoloAction()) is an auto-approval mechanism that bypasses human confirmation for tool calls classified as low or medium risk. The problem: that risk classification is based on heuristics, not context. A medium-risk shell command in a dev environment is very different from one running against a production database. We help teams define explicit approval gates that override auto-approval for sensitive operations.

faqs.question: How should we vet MCP servers before adding them to Claude Code?
faqs.answer: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers extend what Claude Code can do - but a malicious or compromised MCP server can exfiltrate context, execute code, or escalate permissions. Before adding any MCP server you should: verify the source and maintainer, review the server's declared tool definitions, run it in an isolated network environment, and restrict the filesystem and network permissions available to it. We conduct MCP server security reviews as part of our audit.

faqs.question: Does Claude Code send my code to Anthropic's servers?
faqs.answer: Yes. Code, file contents, and terminal output included in the context window are sent to Anthropic's API for inference. This is expected behavior, but it means your intellectual property, internal architecture, and potentially sensitive logic travels over the network. Enterprise teams should configure .claudeignore to exclude proprietary modules, evaluate Anthropic's data handling policies against their compliance requirements, and consider whether on-premise alternatives are needed for the most sensitive workstreams.

faqs.question: What exactly is in scope for the Claude Code audit?
faqs.answer: Our audit reviews: .claudeignore configuration and file access scope, shell command policies and approval gates, MCP server inventory and trust posture, secrets exposure risk in the current workflow, AI-generated code quality and vulnerability patterns, developer practices around context hygiene, and CI/CD integration for automated security scanning of AI-generated output. You receive a written report with prioritized findings and a hardened configuration package.

faqs.question: How long does an AI code security engagement take?
faqs.answer: A focused audit for a team of up to 20 developers typically runs 1-2 weeks from kickoff to final report. Hardening implementation adds 1 week. Training workshops are delivered in a single day. Ongoing monitoring is a retainer that starts after the initial engagement. We can scope a faster 3-day rapid assessment for teams with urgent compliance deadlines.

faqs.question: How is this different from Claude Code's built-in /security-review command or a generic penetration test?
faqs.answer: The built-in /security-review command and its GitHub Action catch code-level issues in a given pull request, things like SQL injection, missing input validation, or an outdated dependency. A generic penetration test targets your application's attack surface: APIs, auth flows, network exposure. Our audit covers a different layer entirely: whether Claude Code itself is configured safely across your team, meaning file access scope, MCP server trust, shell command approval gates, and hook policies. A codebase can pass every pull request review and every pentest and still expose a live prompt injection or credential leak vector through the agent's own configuration. Most teams get the most value running the built-in review on every pull request and our audit on the underlying setup.

faqs.question: How is a Claude Code security audit priced?
faqs.answer: Pricing is scoped to team size and the number of MCP servers and integrations in use, not a fixed rate card. On the free 30-minute call we ask about your current setup and give you a specific quote before any paid work starts, in line with the audit and harden timelines described above.

faqs.question: How can I audit code generated by Claude Code or Copilot for compliance?
faqs.answer: Treat AI-generated code as untrusted input: scan every AI-assisted pull request with SAST in CI, require human review before merge, and keep a record of which agent touched which files. We set up that pipeline, then map the findings to the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 so your compliance team has a named framework to point to.

faqs.question: How do I record or audit what AI coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor do?
faqs.answer: Log every tool call at the configuration layer. In Claude Code, PreToolUse and PostToolUse hooks can record and block commands before and after they run, and approval gates stop destructive or network-touching actions until a developer confirms. We configure those hooks, add alerting on policy violations, and document how each action traces back to a developer.

faqs.question: What can an AI coding agent touch on a developer machine?
faqs.answer: With default settings, anything the developer account can reach: every readable file including .env and private keys, the shell, the network, and whatever each MCP server exposes. That context can be sent to the model provider with each prompt. The audit maps that access for every developer setup, then the hardening pass cuts it down to what the work actually needs.

faqs.question: Do you audit small teams or only enterprise engineering orgs?
faqs.answer: Both. Pricing is scoped to team size and the number of MCP servers and integrations in use, so a five-person team pays for a smaller scope than a fifty-person one. Tell us how many developers use AI coding tools and which ones on the free call, and you get a specific quote before any paid work starts.

faqs.question: Do we have to stop using Claude Code during the audit?
faqs.answer: No. The audit reads your configuration, hooks, .claudeignore, MCP server inventory and developer practices while your team keeps shipping. Hardening changes are documented and version-controlled, so they roll out like any other config change and can be reviewed before they land. Training is a single day, scheduled around your release calendar.

faqs.question: Who is this audit not for?
faqs.answer: Teams that do not use AI coding agents yet, and teams that only need an application penetration test of their APIs and auth flows. This audit covers how the agent itself is configured and what it can reach. If that is not your risk, a standard pentest or the built-in /security-review command on each pull request is the better fit.

faqs.question: Can you review an AI agent before it goes to production, not just coding tools?
faqs.answer: Yes. We review custom AI coding agents and internally built assistants for the same risks: tool permissions, prompt injection, secrets handling and sandbox isolation. For agents that act on business systems, start with our production readiness checklist, then book the call and we scope which checks your agent needs before launch.

sections.title: What CRM implementation services include
body: What it is

CRM implementation services cover four jobs: configuring the CRM around how you actually sell, migrating records from the old system or spreadsheets, connecting the tools that feed it, and automating the upkeep so the data stays usable. Most projects fail on the fourth job, not the first three.

A CRM nobody maintains becomes a CRM nobody trusts. The same person gets added twice from a web form, a list import and a rep typing by hand. Nobody merges the duplicates because it is nobody's job. Two reps work the same account without knowing it, a new lead sits unrouted for days, and reps go back to private spreadsheets. It is an ownership problem more than a software problem.

So we build the ownership into the system. Stages and the fields reps must fill become dropdowns instead of free text. Duplicates are blocked at entry and merged on a schedule. Deals with no activity get flagged. One named person gets a short weekly digest instead of a cleanup project every quarter.

sections.title: The model came from Palantir , and frontier AI labs adopted it for the same reason.
body: Why this role exists

Palantir embedded roughly 120 engineers directly with JPMorgan in 2009, because the data was too sensitive and the workflow too specific for a product handed off remotely ( source ). The pattern stuck: a model or a product alone does not produce a working result inside someone else's stack. Somebody has to sit with the mess and build the thing that closes the gap.

Frontier AI labs hit the same wall. OpenAI's own forward deployed engineering team grew from 2 to 39 people in a single year, targeting problems worth tens of millions to low billions, because roughly 95% of enterprise AI deployments never make it to production ( source ). In 2026, OpenAI went further and stood up a dedicated deployment company through the Tomoro acquisition, embedding engineers with adopters including HP, Intuit, Oracle, and State Farm ( source ).
We are not affiliated with and do not partner with Palantir or OpenAI. They are cited here as the origin and market context for the FDE model, not as our clients.

faqs.question: What is a forward deployed engineer (FDE)?
faqs.answer: A forward deployed engineer is an engineer who embeds inside a customer's team and writes production code on top of a product, rather than advising from the outside. The model started at Palantir, where engineers embedded on-site with government and defense customers whose data was too sensitive to hand off remotely.

faqs.question: How is an FDE different from a consultant?
faqs.answer: A consultant is accountable for a recommendation. An FDE is accountable for the shipped result. FDEs write production code themselves, embed for weeks at a time, and use evaluation-driven development instead of a slide deck to earn trust.

faqs.question: How is an FDE different from staff augmentation?
faqs.answer: Staff augmentation places a person against your hours and org chart. An FDE is placed against an outcome: a workflow that needs to run, an agent that needs to hit a quality bar. Same embedded model, different accountability.

faqs.question: Do I need a forward deployed engineer or an AI strategy consultant?
faqs.answer: If you already know what you want built and need someone to build and ship it inside your stack, that is an FDE. If you need help deciding what to build first, start with AI strategy consulting, then bring in an FDE to execute.

sections.title: What a GTM engineering agency does
body: What it is

A GTM engineering agency builds the systems behind outbound instead of renting you a list. The work is six jobs run in sequence: find the people, spot who is buying right now, identify who is on your site, reach out, log and route every reply, and feed content back into new signals. No single tool does all six, and most of the real engineering is the deduplication, routing and suppression logic between them.

Signal-based selling replaces guessing who might have a problem with noticing who just showed it. Someone is promoted into a budget-holding role, their company posts three new sales roles, or they read your pricing page and leave. A signal tool notices, an enrichment table finds and verifies the work email and checks the person is not already in an open deal, and the sending tool uses the signal as the reason for the message.

body: What it is

The role sits between sales, marketing and engineering. Sales wants better targets and less admin. Marketing wants signal to turn into pipeline. Neither team has the time to build the plumbing, and a spreadsheet plus a sequencing tool stops scaling at some point.

In practice the work is five things. Capturing signals such as site visits, job changes and product usage. Enriching accounts and contacts so the data is usable. sections.title: What an MCP development engagement delivers
body: What it is

MCP is a protocol, not a product. The value is in the design of the server: which tools it exposes, how they are described so a model picks the right one, what each is allowed to touch, and what happens on failure.

Public examples often expose a whole API as tools. That floods the model with choices and gives it more power than the task needs. We design narrow tools around real jobs, such as look up an order or draft a reply, and enforce limits on the server side.
We work at the server and integration level, and connect it to clients such as Claude and Claude Code. We do not claim to run a hosted MCP marketplace.

sections.title: What n8n enterprise automation involves
body: What it is

Scale in n8n is mostly architecture. Queue mode splits the main process from workers that pull jobs from Redis, and PostgreSQL replaces the default database. That lets you add workers for load and restart parts without stopping everything.

Governance is the other half. Who can edit production workflows, how changes move from development to production, where secrets live and how you see failures. Some access-control features, such as SSO and advanced roles, depend on n8n's paid plans. We tell you which apply before you commit, and check the current n8n documentation for each.
We do not claim n8n or our services carry a compliance certification. We build the controls your auditors ask about and document them.

faqs.question: What is enterprise automation?
faqs.answer: Enterprise automation is running business processes across several teams and systems on one governed platform, instead of each team keeping its own scripts. It adds what single-team automation skips: access roles, secrets handling, change control between environments, execution logs, and a setup that keeps running when one part fails. On n8n that means queue mode with workers on PostgreSQL, designed for high availability.

faqs.question: How do you set up high availability for self-hosted n8n?
faqs.answer: Run n8n in queue mode: the main process hands executions to a Redis queue, several workers pull from it, and PostgreSQL stores workflows and execution data. Run more than one worker so losing one does not stop executions, back up PostgreSQL and test a restore, then test worker loss and a bad deploy before production. Which HA options your plan includes changes over time, so we check n8n's current documentation with you first.

faqs.question: What is queue mode?
faqs.answer: It separates the main n8n process from worker processes. Workers pull executions from a Redis queue, so you can add workers for load and restart them without stopping the whole system. It runs with PostgreSQL as the database.

faqs.question: Which access features need a paid n8n plan?
faqs.answer: Some features such as SSO and advanced role controls depend on n8n's paid plans. Plans change, so we check n8n's current documentation with you before design and tell you what applies.

faqs.question: Are you SOC 2 certified, or is n8n?
faqs.answer: We do not claim certifications we cannot show. We build controls such as access roles, change control and logs that your auditors can review, and we document them.

faqs.question: What does it cost?
faqs.answer: Scoped after a discovery call, because it depends on volume, availability needs and the number of workflows to migrate. Infrastructure costs are yours and depend on your cloud.

faqs.question: Who runs it after go-live?
faqs.answer: Your team from our runbook, or us under a maintenance plan covering updates, monitoring and fixes.

sections.title: What product scoping actually covers
body: What it is

Scoping is not a slide deck. The core of the sprint is a working prototype of the riskiest part of your product: can the model actually do the job on your real inputs, at a cost per task that leaves you a margin? Everything else in the plan hangs on that answer.

Around the prototype we map the boring 70% that makes AI products real: data access, auth, queues, rate limits, cost caps, and the human-review path for when the model is wrong. That is where most estimates lie, so it is where we spend the mapping time.
You get the findings either way. If the honest answer is "do not build this yet", we say so and show you what would have to change. That outcome costs you a sprint instead of a failed project.

sections.title: What the audit covers
body: What it is

We walk your core funnels the way a new user does: signup, first value, the feature you charge for, and the path back. Every friction point gets logged with where it sits in the funnel and how many users hit it, from your analytics where they exist and from instrumented sessions where they do not.
The heuristic pass covers the unglamorous killers: unclear empty states, dead ends after errors, forms that fight the user, mobile breakage, and copy that assumes knowledge a new user does not have.

The deliverable is a fix list ordered by users-affected times effort, written so your own team can ship it. We are engineers, not a redesign studio: the audit exists to make your product convert, not to sell you a rebrand.

sections.title: What a generative AI development company builds
body: What it is

A generative AI development company builds software where a large language model writes, answers, summarises or decides as part of the product. In practice that means three kinds of work: retrieval systems that answer from your own documents, agents that read and act in your tools, and LLM features shipped inside an existing product.

The model is the easy part to buy. What takes the work is everything around it: which documents it can see, which actions it may take, what it costs per run, and how you know an answer is right. We write those down first, collect real examples with the answers a good result should give, and test every version against them.

We do not train foundation models. We build on Claude and OpenAI models through your approved accounts, chosen per task after testing, in TypeScript and Python. If a non-generative approach or an off-the-shelf tool does the job better, we say so.

faqs.question: What does a generative AI development company do?
faqs.answer: A generative AI development company builds software where a large language model produces the output: answers from your documents, drafted text, summaries or actions taken by an agent. The work covers the use case, the data the model may see, testing against real examples, and running the system in production with logging and cost tracking.

faqs.question: How do I choose a generative AI development company?
faqs.answer: Ask four things. Will they build a test set from your real examples and show you the results? Can they show a system that is still live in production? Who owns the code and the model accounts? How do they handle a model update from the provider? Our answers: a test set in week 2, code in your repositories, and monitoring plus an optional maintenance plan after release.

faqs.question: Is this different from custom AI development?
faqs.answer: This page covers products built on large language models: RAG, agents and generative features. Our custom AI development company page covers the wider set, including matching, prediction and internal tools that may not use an LLM at all.

faqs.question: Do you train or fine-tune models on our data?
faqs.answer: Usually not. We use retrieval, tools and prompts against your data through approved model routes. Fine-tuning is a separate decision and only makes sense when testing shows it helps.

faqs.question: Which models do you use?
faqs.answer: Mostly Claude and OpenAI models, chosen per task after testing on your examples. A smaller, cheaper model often handles routing or classification steps, with a larger one where the answer quality needs it.

faqs.question: What does it cost?
faqs.answer: Scoped after a discovery call, because cost follows the systems, the data access and the review steps. Use the AI agent cost calculator to estimate running costs. Placement of an embedded engineer starts from $60,000/year.

faqs.question: Who owns the code and the data?
faqs.answer: You do. We build in your repositories and cloud accounts, use your model accounts, and hand over documentation and a runbook.
